title: Career Sprint & Onboarding Toolkit for People Ops and Managers
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary:
This playbook bundles a repeatable 'Career Sprint' program with an integrated onboarding toolkit aimed at accelerating impact for new hires and enabling managers to drive development and role progression. It summarizes role bands, core competencies, the 90-day onboarding checklist, benefits highlights relevant during the first year, and the internal tools access matrix required for typical job families (Engineering, Product, Sales, Customer Success).

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-impact for new hires, standardize first-line manager handoffs, and create a lightweight, measurable career-development cadence (the Career Sprint).
- Scope: Applies to all full-time and long-term contractors across Product, Engineering, and GTM teams. Excludes executive-level bespoke onboarding (handled by People Ops leadership).

Quick links and templates (internal):
- New Hire Manager Handoff form: /templates/manager-handoff
- Career Sprint template & example sprint goals: /templates/career-sprint
- Onboarding checklist (role-specific): /tools/onboarding/checklists
- Badge & Access request quick form: /tools/access/request

Section 1 — Role ladder snapshot (summary table)
Note: This is a concise, role-family-agnostic snapshot. For full competency maps, see related pages.

| Band | Typical titles | Core expectations (1-line) | Promotion signals | Typical timeline |
|------|----------------|----------------------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| IC2  | Associate / Junior | Executes tasks with close guidance | Consistent delivery of assigned work, learning velocity | 6–12 months |
| IC3  | Senior / Mid | Independently owns features, mentors juniors | High-impact deliverables, cross-team collaboration | 12–24 months |
| IC4  | Staff / Lead | Shapes technical direction, drives cross-team outcomes | Strategic impact, mentoring & design leadership | 18–36 months |
| IC5+ | Principal / Director (individual contributor track) | Company-level influence, long-term domain ownership | Repeated strategic wins, org influence | Variable |

Section 2 — Career Sprint (design and cadence)
Goal: Provide a 3-month focused development loop aligned to role expectations and business objectives.

Core elements:
1. Sprint kickoff (week 0): manager and IC agree on 2–3 measurable outcomes (impact metric + skill growth target).
2. Mid-sprint checkpoint (week 6): asynchronous progress note + 30-minute sync.
3. End-sprint review (week 12): demo or write-up, manager assessment vs. success criteria, and 1:1 to set next sprint.
4. Calibration: People Ops collects anonymized sprint outcomes quarterly to identify cross-team blockers and learning program needs.

Example success criteria (engineering IC3 -> IC4 sprint):
- Outcome metric: Reduce feature latency by 20% for the Payments API (measured via staging perf tests).
- Skill target: Lead a cross-team RFC and demonstrate constructive stakeholder negotiation.

Section 3 — First 90 days onboarding checklist (compact)
Manager responsibilities (before day 1):
- Complete Manager Handoff form and confirm workstation, accounts, manager buddy.
- Schedule day-1 orientation and first-week 1:1 slots.
- Approve initial access requests (see access matrix).

Day 0–7 (orientation & access):
- Paperwork completion (payroll, security training).
- Tool access granted: Slack, Okta, email, GitHub/Repo, CI dashboards, internal wikis.
- Role-specific training: codebase tour, product demo, customer context session.

Days 8–30 (context & small wins):
- Assign first small deliverable with defined acceptance criteria.
- Pair with a buddy for daily syncs for first two weeks.
- Schedule cross-functional introductions: SRE/infra, Product, Support.

Days 31–90 (ownership & career sprint):
- Launch first Career Sprint (see Section 2).
- 30/60/90 feedback sessions: gather written feedback from 3 collaborators.
- Quarterly learning plan drafted and agreed.

Section 4 — Benefits highlights (first-year focus)
- Healthcare: Primary enrollment window is within 30 days of start. Summary plan comparison is in Benefits Portal.
- Parental leave: Primary caregiver full pay for 14 weeks; secondary caregiver 6 weeks (policy exceptions via People Ops).
- Professional development: $2,000 learning stipend in the first 12 months and quarterly cohort workshops.
- Hybrid work & office stipend: $200/month equipment allowance for the first 6 months; flexible office hoteling instructions in Internal Tools.

Section 5 — Internal tools access matrix (text table)
Purpose: Quick view of who typically needs which system on hire. Final access must be approved by managers in the Manager Handoff form.

| Role Family | Slack/Okta | GitHub | Prod Console | Billing Portal | Jira | Confluence | Internal DBs |
|-------------|-----------|--------|------------|----------------|------|-----------|--------------|
| Engineering  | Yes       | Yes    | Limited dev | No             | Yes  | Yes       | Role-based   |
| Product      | Yes       | Yes(r)/No | Dashboards | Billing read   | Yes  | Yes       | Read-only    |
| Sales/GTM    | Yes       | No     | No         | Full           | Yes  | Yes       | CRM-only     |
| CS / Support | Yes       | No     | Incident ops | Billing read  | Yes  | Yes       | Support-only |

Section 6 — Manager guide: first-week playbook (top-line)
1. Day 1: 30–45 minute welcome + team intro; review role scope and first-week goals.
2. End of week 1: hand-off technical/functional resources and ensure access; schedule 30/60/90 meetings.
3. By week 4: confirm first deliverable acceptance criteria; ensure buddy pairing; check benefits enrollments.

Section 7 — Promotion and calibration process (how Career Sprints feed into promotions)
- Evidence-based promotions: Managers should rely on sprint outcomes, documented impact, and calibration notes from peers.
- Promotion packet: 1-page impact summary, manager recommendation, 3 peer statements, and sprint artifacts (RFC, demo recording, metrics).
- Calibration cycle: Quarterly cross-functional calibration; People Ops facilitates and publishes decisions and rationale to managers.

Section 8 — FAQs and common gotchas
Q: Can contractors run Career Sprints?
A: Long-term contractors (>6 months) can participate; promotion mechanics do not apply, but skill-planning and learning budgets can be made available case-by-case.

Q: What if access is delayed beyond day 3?
A: Escalate via AccessOps channel with manager ping. People Ops tracks SLAs (goal: 72 hours for standard access).

Section 9 — Ownership, review and metrics
- Owner: People Ops (document steward: Priya Nair).
- Metrics tracked: median time-to-first-merge, % of hires with access within 72 hours, % of sprints with published outcomes, manager satisfaction (quarterly pulse).
- Review cadence: Annual doc review or post-major process change; People Ops and two reviewer managers must sign off.

Appendix A — Quick templates and commands
- Manager Handoff link: /templates/manager-handoff (copy the template before use).
- Example career sprint goals: /templates/career-sprint/examples.
- Onboarding / access request CLI (internal):
  - Request access: curl -X POST https://access.internal/api/request -d '{"user": "<email>", "roles": ["github","slack"]}'

If you are a manager or new hire with questions not covered here, open a ticket at People Ops or join the #people-ops Slack channel.
